title: arxiv_2606.20542v1
universal_lens: The CalTennis benchmark formalizes the mapping from a high-dimensional, multi-view spatiotemporal manifold of expert athletic motion to a lower-dimensional monocular representation. This structural unification exposes fundamental isomorphisms between biomechanical state-space constraints and the geometric ambiguities inherent in single-camera depth recovery.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs multi-view synchronized recordings as a label-free ground truth prior for Bayesian inference. By treating overlapping camera views as independent stochastic observations, we construct conformal prediction sets that rigorously quantify the epistemic uncertainty of monocular-to-3D pose estimators under real-world occlusions and varying depths.
gse_mapping: GSE translates the recovered kinematic states into situational reasoning graphs. The primitives map continuous biomechanical trajectories—specifically footwork and stability—into discrete state-transitions. This allows the engine to evaluate tactical execution by detecting inconsistencies in metric-scale depth and ground contact across sequential frames.

primitives.name: Monocular Depth Instability Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Benchmarking state-of-the-art monocular-to-3D pose methods on CalTennis, we find that while 3D joint angle recovery is now quite accurate, all models struggle to estimate depth and foot contact consistently.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Joint angles (dimensionless/radians), Metric-scale depth estimates (meters), Frame rate (Hz)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes standard perspective projection and smooth biomechanical transitions between consecutive video frames.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down during rapid, unconstrained athletic movements where depth cues are ambiguous and parallax is insufficient for monocular triangulation.

layer2.mapping: Maps the ill-posed inverse graphics problem directly to GSI's depth uncertainty quantification, highlighting the failure of purely visual priors without multi-view constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Variance in estimated 3D body position across temporally adjacent frames.

primitives.name: Footwork and Stability Metric Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: We further propose two novel performance metrics – footwork and stability – as well as qualitatively study body shape inconsistency.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Footwork score (dimensionless), Stability index (dimensionless), Body proportions (meters)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes rigid body dynamics for limb lengths and consistent gravitational interaction with the court surface.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when severe motion blur or complete occlusion prevents reliable detection of foot-court intersections.

layer2.mapping: Serves as the foundational kernel for GSE's action analysis, converting raw coordinate data into actionable biomechanical performance indicators.
layer2.telemetry: Consistency of foot contact detection across multiple synchronized camera views.

primitives.name: Biomechanical Error Propagation Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Across all of these, the utility of pose estimation is bounded by its accuracy: small errors in joint position, depth, or ground contact propagate directly into the biomechanical, behavioral, and narrative conclusions that downstream systems draw.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Joint position error (meters), Ground contact error (boolean/meters), Downstream conclusion variance (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a differentiable, non-linear mapping from low-level kinematic states to high-level biomechanical or behavioral outputs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when minor spatial perturbations cross a decision boundary, causing catastrophic divergence in inferred force vectors or tactical intent.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the sensitivity analysis in GSI's conformal inference, dictating the required precision of the base pose estimator to maintain valid downstream confidence intervals.
layer2.telemetry: Gradient of output narrative/behavioral classification with respect to input joint coordinate noise.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation of sovereign primitives from the CalTennis benchmark begins by recognizing the fundamental duality between high-fidelity multi-view capture and the constrained reality of monocular observation. Mathematically, the multi-view setup provides an overdetermined system of equations for 3D reconstruction, effectively acting as a label-free ground truth. We define the Monocular Depth Instability Operator by analyzing the residual variance between the true multi-view consensus and the monocular estimate. While angular configurations (joint angles) remain relatively robust due to strong 2D silhouette priors, the metric-scale depth dimension suffers from a lack of absolute scale cues in single views, leading to rapid, unrealistic jumps in the reconstructed state space.

This instability directly informs the Footwork and Stability Metric Kernel. In biomechanics, stability is intrinsically linked to the precise location of the center of mass relative to the base of support (foot contact). If the depth operator fails, the inferred ground contact points fluctuate wildly, rendering any calculation of balance or force distribution meaningless. Consequently, we introduce the Biomechanical Error Propagation Operator. This operator models the non-linear amplification of low-level pixel or metric errors into high-level semantic failures. A few centimeters of error in knee depth can completely invert the calculated torque or misclassify a player's readiness state. The dualities here lie between local geometric accuracy and global biomechanical plausibility; the failure modes are not merely statistical noise but systematic violations of physical constraints, such as inconsistent body shapes or phantom foot contacts, which expose the limitations of current deep learning priors when extrapolated to extreme, unconstrained athletic motions.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The lineage of these operators traces back to the classical structure-from-motion (SfM) problems in computer vision, which sought to recover 3D geometry from 2D projections. Historically, this evolved through marker-based motion capture (MOCAP), which provided gold-standard accuracy but at immense cost and ecological invalidity. The shift toward markerless, in-the-wild pose estimation represents a retrocausal pressure from applied domains like sports analytics and robotics, demanding that mathematical models abandon controlled laboratory assumptions in favor of robust, generalizable priors capable of handling the chaotic, high-frequency dynamics of real-world human movement.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling the opposing agents in this context involves viewing the monocular pose estimator as an actor attempting to infer hidden 3D states from incomplete, noisy sensory data. The 'opponent' is the inherent ambiguity of the visual field—occlusions, lighting changes, and perspective collapses. The estimator must anticipate the biomechanical intentions of the athlete (e.g., a sudden lunge or jump) to regularize its predictions. However, when the estimator's internal model of human motion is too rigid or biased toward common, low-energy poses, it fails to track the extreme articulations of expert athletes, leading to the observed inconsistencies in depth and foot contact.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity and leakage veto conditions are critical when fusing these primitives. We must veto any downstream biomechanical conclusion if the underlying depth estimates exhibit high temporal frequency noise indicative of monocular instability rather than true athletic acceleration. Furthermore, we enforce a leakage veto: the body shape parameters inferred from one view must not uncontrollably bias the pose estimation in another view. If the estimated limb lengths vary systematically across synchronized cameras, the multi-view consistency check fails, triggering a veto on the entire sequence to prevent corrupted data from polluting the GSI conformal prediction sets.
